A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete, readable main text, references, and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision-language matching experiments, solver comparisons, unsupervised classification results, and appendix ablations and alignment analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised numerical and graphical results in both the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The factorized Hahn-Grant algorithm, primal heuristics, embedding construction, and classification procedure remain unchanged. The corrected subset-selection summation expresses the full candidate-set selection already described in v1; it does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same matching and classification tasks using CIFAR-10, CINIC-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100, with CocoCaptions also used in the alignment diagnostics. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding solver comparisons retain Random, LocalCKA, OT, FAQ, MPOpt, and Gurobi where previously included. The metric comparisons and component ablations also retain their comparison groups. LocalCKA was already evaluated in Figure 6; its newly visible curve does not add a comparator.

E3.justification: Table 1's reported configuration switches from CLIP/all-mpnet-base-v2 on CINIC-10 to DINOv2/All-Roberta-large-v1 on CIFAR-10. Both configurations already occur in Table 7, so this changes the highlighted comparison without expanding the evaluation grid. Appendix E retains the splits, sampling, problem sizes, and computational budgets.

E4.justification: The existing metric comparison in Table 3, component ablations in Tables 4–5, and shuffling and random-network diagnostics in Figures 7–9 receive revised evidence. These revisions affect answers about metric superiority and component tradeoffs, but introduce no new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: The stated repeated-run procedures remain unchanged, including 20 seeds for small-scale matching and classification, five for component ablations, and 100 shuffling trials per level. Standard deviations and shaded uncertainty bands already appear in v1; revised spreads do not constitute a new reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results change substantially across Tables 1–7 and the empirical figures. In Table 3, CINIC-10 CKA accuracy changes from 40% to 80%, while GW changes from 77% to 79%, reversing their ranking. In matched Table 7 settings, CLIP/all-mpnet-base-v2 on CINIC-10 changes from 60% to 50% for the proposed solver. Table 2's best classification accuracy changes from 51.5% to 51.1%. Table 1's 60%-to-100% difference uses different configurations and is not a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Equation 13 corrects the subset-selection objective's summation limit from N to L, consistent with selecting N classes from L candidates. This repairs the mathematical formulation. The appendix equivalence proof and optimal-transport derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a QAP formulation and solver, selection of suitable matching problems, feasibility of blind alignment, and an unsupervised classifier. Revised supporting results do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B narrows GW's claimed advantage from higher accuracy on both datasets to comparable or higher accuracy. Appendix D.3 removes the explanation for factorization increasing the objective and adds a tradeoff between improved primal solutions and slightly worse bounds. The main applicability and scalability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices D.2 and E retain the implementation libraries, stopping tolerances, preprocessing, model sources, computational arrangements, and K-Means initialization details. Code-related access information is unchanged. Experimental-detail paragraphs move across page boundaries without adding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to prior alignment and QAP methods remain unchanged. Added inline citations in Table 6 point to works already cited in v1; reference backlink changes do not add literature.

P1.justification: Edits are concentrated in results paragraphs, qualifications, and captions; the section and appendix organization remains intact. Section 5 changes the vision-model count from 33 to 32, matching the count already stated in v1's Appendix E, rather than documenting a removed model.

P2.justification: The figure and table inventory remains unchanged. Presentation edits include moving Figure 4's legend, displaying LocalCKA in Figure 6, changing Figure 11's vertical scale, reversing Table 7's language-model column groups, and adjusting table typography and page flow. Updated plotted values are separately assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Equation 13 and qualifies some interpretations, but the extensive empirical revisions are unexplained and incompletely reconciled with the text. Table 3 still calls GW the best metric despite CKA scoring 80% versus GW's 79% on CINIC-10, and Section 5.3 retains a setup inconsistent with the revised Table 1 caption. These corrections and newly introduced reporting inconsistencies leave the net quality effect uncertain.
